title: Single dispatcher unifies REST and MCP transports
context: Agent gateways and remote orchestrators need to use hunch tools via MCP without stdio; managed agent runtimes (Bedrock AgentCore, etc.) require HTTP-addressable tool targets alongside decision record state. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_91e6074b66 (Capability pages for functionality shipped in the current release must state that it ships today and must not retain the stale banner 'In development for the next release.').
decision: Implement MCP over streamable HTTP (POST /nuryel/v1/mcp) with one shared dispatcher in src/serve/app.ts. REST and MCP tools use identical credentials (bearer/DPoP), grants, write lock, and refusal semantics — enforced by architecture, not duplication.
consequences: Transport cannot diverge — changes to grants or lock behavior automatically apply to both REST and MCP
Enables agent gateways to add hunch as state layer without separate orchestration
HTTP becomes a supported tool transport, opening path to managed runtime integration
Requires web-standard transport bridging without pulling production dependencies (node-server stays dev-only)
alternatives_rejected: Separate MCP server implementation — risk of divergence between REST and MCP behavior
Stdio-only MCP transport — does not work for remote orchestrators or managed runtimes
Embedding HTTP client library in production code — fails dependency audit
